about: The atmosphere classes of the new world (walk 5): each class is a real tropical atmosphere (docs/research/nw-02-walk5-atmosphere.md section 1) built Skyrim's way (section 3): a set of our own weathers copied from the vanilla regional set of the same family (Bethesda's MA marsh, FF fall forest, RE Reach, CO coast sets) and re-coloured. A colour slot keeps Bethesda's luminance for its weather and time of day and takes the class's hue (sun from its colour temperature in kelvin; haze, fill, ground and sky as written here); fog distances are Skyrim's base weathers' (reference_fog) times the class's visibility (relative humidity and aerosol, section 1.8). Band rows shift a region by latitude (section 1.9). tools/newworld/atmosphere.py reads this; docs/design/atmosphere.md is the recipe.

kind_why.fair: sun through humid haze; the dawn mist lives in its Night fog slot and burns off across the climate's sunrise window
kind_why.cloudy: broken cumulus, the commonest tropical day; same dawn mist
kind_why.mist: a fog day: low cloud and mist that does not lift
kind_why.steam: the air after rain: warm, close, sunlit fog rising off wet ground and water

reference_fog.why: Fog distances start from Skyrim's base weathers (the Update.esm winners BM&V's climate lists: Clear 80000 by day, Cloudy 100000, Fog 25000, OvercastRain 15000, StormRain 25000 units) so every class is scaled from one reference by its humidity and aerosol alone; the regional sets' own distances vary for reasons of Skyrim's land (the Reach's clear day is 50000, Hjaalmarch's 90000) and would put the clearest air in the wrong class.

marsh.why: Hjaalmarch's set (REGN WeatherTundraMarsh 0C5855): Bethesda's marsh weathers

forest.why: the Rift's fall-forest set (REGN WeatherFallForest): Bethesda's forest and river-valley weathers, the only set with its own storm

upland.why: the Reach's set (REGN WeatherReach): Bethesda's rocky upland weathers

coast.why: the coast set (REGN WeatherCoast, WeatherCoastFog): Bethesda's sea weathers; its snow replaced by the generic rain and storm

north.why: By the Morrowind border (cells y above -135): the drier edge of the monsoon belt, like the Western Ghats' northern end and the Deccan edge: clearer fair days, harder storms, less steam (section 1.9).

middle.why: The interior: the class as researched.

south.why: The south coast belt (cells y below -185): hottest and most humid, on the Sea of Mists, like Kerala's backwaters and Borneo's south coast: more mist and steam, fewer clear days (section 1.9).

climate.why: One climate per worldspace (the engine has no regional timing). A tropical day is twelve hours with a short twilight: sunset at about 18:20 (section 1.7), the centre of a 16:30-20:30 window, as vanilla's 16:00-20:30 centres on 18:15. The sunrise window runs to 11:00 so the Night fog slot (the dawn mist) lerps to the Day slot through the morning: mist strong at dawn and gone before noon, as valley and river fog burns off by 09:00-10:00 in Borneo and Kerala (section 1.2). The default list is the green marsh's, the province's commonest ground.

blackwater-swamp.name: Blackwater peat swamp
blackwater-swamp.analogue: Borneo's peat swamp forest (Sebangau, Central Kalimantan; Belait, Brunei): tea-black water, stunted forest, the closest air

green-marsh.name: Green marsh and backwater
green-marsh.analogue: Kerala's backwaters and Kuttanad's paddies; Borneo's open freshwater marsh: bright green reed and paddy under a luminous white sky

river-corridor.name: River corridor
river-corridor.analogue: The Kinabatangan and Rajang in Borneo, the Periyar in Kerala: brown rivers in a humid valley, river fog at dawn, storms in the afternoon

rainforest.name: Lowland swamp rainforest
rainforest.analogue: Borneo's lowland dipterocarp forest (Danum Valley, Sabah): closed canopy, green dim light, steam off the canopy at dawn, afternoon thunderstorms

highland.name: Highland and mesa
highland.analogue: The Western Ghats (Munnar, the Nilgiris), Borneo's karst and montane uplands (Mulu, Kinabalu's lower slopes): crisper air, blue layered distance, valley mist below

coast-east.name: East coast (the Padomaic shore)
coast-east.analogue: A windward monsoon coast (the Malabar coast in the south-west monsoon; Sabah's east coast in the north-east monsoon): wind, long swell, overcast and rain off the ocean, silver sea haze

coast-south.name: South coast (the Sea of Mists)
coast-south.analogue: Borneo's south coast and the Sundarbans' creeks: sea mist most mornings, warm milky haze over mangrove and mud

coast-west.name: West coast (Topal Bay)
coast-west.analogue: A sheltered bay coast facing the sunset (Kerala's lagoons at Alappuzha, Sabah's west coast at Kota Kinabalu): sunny mornings, sea breeze, squalls, fiery sunsets over the water

island.name: Islands
island.analogue: Small tropical islands in clean sea air (the Lakshadweep, Sabah's offshore islands): bright light, turquoise shallows, passing showers, the clearest air
